name: ad-groups
description:
Small ad groups of one intent: phrases that are duplicates by meaning of each other share a group.

Two phrases of the same refining words and close vectors (the rule of `dupes_meaning`) are one intent, and a chain of such pairs makes one group. A group of more than `max_size` phrases is split: the first phrase left takes the `max_size` phrases nearest to it, and so on, so the same input gives the same groups. Equal phrases are one phrase. The groups are numbered from 1 in the order of their first rows. The columns: ad_group and ad_group_name; every phrase gets them, an empty cell gets none.

max_size: the most phrases in an ad group, 1 or more; a larger group is split by vector. Without it no group is split.
freq: the column of the frequencies of the phrases in the current table; the ad group is named after its most frequent phrase. Without it, after its first phrase.
neutral: the Human's non-refining words for --kind meaning, as @FILE or @NAME of a list; they add to the bundled list @meaning/neutral. Words are compared by lemma.
synonyms: a file with the columns word and synonyms, as the step `synonyms` gives, for --kind meaning; a word and its synonyms are the same word. The file is read like `read` does.
home: the name of the home city for --kind meaning; its word is non-refining, another city's is not.
threshold: the similarity from 0 to 1 two phrases need to be one intent, for --kind meaning. Without it the threshold of the model.
model: the encoder, pulled once with `semkit models pull NAME`: e5-small, bge-m3, potion, or hf:<id> of a model of the Hugging Face hub. Without --threshold the step takes the threshold of the model; a hub model has none.

The step adds the columns ad_group and ad_group_name right after the working column; the rows stay.

Example: semkit read core.csv ad-groups --max-size 20 --freq freq write out.csv
